title: 第十一章 十二第十二章 麻雀
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
第十一章十二
苏尘从密室里出来的时候，天色已经暗了。
他在出口处站了几息，等眼睛适应光线的变化，然后弯腰把活动的石板盖好，再把床板拖回原位。一切恢复原状，从外面看，这间正屋跟任何一间普通的乡间住房没有任何区别。
他推开门，走到院子里，深深吸了一口傍晚的空气。
刚才在密室里坐了将近两个时辰，引动龙脉气息走完了八个小周天。收功的那一刻，他清楚地感觉到丹田里那团元气猛地一沉，像是终于跨过了一道无形的门槛——淬体境中期，他正式踏入了。
那一瞬间的感觉很微妙。像是一直在爬一段缓坡，爬了很久都感觉不到变化，但就在某个不经意的瞬间忽然回头一看，才发现自己已经比出发时高了很大一截。丹田里的元气不再像之前那样需要刻意维持才不散，而是自然而然地聚拢在一起，自成一个稳定的循环。虽然量还不多，但质已经不一样了——像是把一团松散的面絮揉成了一个光滑的面团。
从入境到中期，花了整整两年。
这个速度说不上快。纳气法本来就是市面上最烂的货色，能量的吸收效率低得可怜。起步的前半年更不用提——经脉又窄又弱，每引导一丝能量入体都像用一根细吸管喝水，费半天劲只能吸上来一小口，稍不留神就断了。那段时间他每天雷打不动地练足两个时辰，但丹田里的元气增长几乎肉眼看不出来。有好几次，他练完之后坐在蒲团上闭眼内视，丹田里空空荡荡的，跟没练过一样。他明白这是必经之路——前世曹钦练的秘藏功法起步时也慢，但那是太监专用路线，跟正常路子不同。没想到换了纳气法，起步比前世还难熬。有时候练完一整晚，第二天气感反而比前一天还淡，像是好不容易攒下来的一点又漏掉了。他心里清楚这是经脉还没适应能量流动的正常现象。有好几个深夜，他独自坐在密室的蒲团上，感受着丹田里那若有若无的一丝元气，忍不住想起前世曹钦巅峰时期那种举手投足间元气奔涌如江河的感觉。对比之下，现在的自己简直像一个拿着木剑的孩子望着山巅的剑客。但他也就是想想，叹一口气，然后收回心思继续运功。他知道急没用，这条路他从前世就已经明白了——根基不牢，后面走不远。
真正开始见效是半年以后的事。经脉在日复一日的打磨中逐渐拓宽，就像一条被人反复踩踏的小路，走着走着就宽了。能量在体内的流动越来越顺畅，不再动不动就断。同样是两个时辰，最初只能勉强走完一两个小周天，半年后能走到四五个。然后是六个、七个——到最近一个月，已经稳定在八个了。丹田里的那团元气也从最初若有若无的一丝，长到了现在小指粗细的一团，运转起来有一种扎实的厚重感，不像刚开始那样风一吹就要散。
密室底下那条重叠龙脉也功不可没。虽然每次引动的量微乎其微，但两年日积月累下来，那一点一滴的差距就在不知不觉中显现出来了。像是一条涓涓细流，水量不大，但常年不断，总能把田地浇透。他有时候会想，如果没有这条龙脉，单靠纳气法硬磨，淬体境中期恐怕还要再多花两年。这条马场地下的秘密，大概是他这辈子捡到的最大便宜了。
按这个势头，淬体境圆满应该不需要再花两年了。他心里大致估算了一下——中期到圆满比入境到中期要快，因为经脉已经通了，后面的路只是积累的问题。一年半左右应该能摸到圆满的门槛。到时候就该考虑突破凝元境的事了。凝元之后是开脉，然后是铸基。
铸基境需要中品功法。他现在手里那本无名残本倒是中品，但缺了关键几页，而且看起来跟血修门派有瓜葛，练不练得、什么时候练、怎么练，都得从长计议。不过那是以后的事。先把眼前这一步踩实了再说。万丈高楼平地起——这话他前世就懂了，但这辈子才真正做得到。
苏尘走下台阶，在暮色中活动了一下肩膀，在院子里随意走了一圈。
两年下来，马场已经完全变了一个模样。围墙高耸结实，青砖勾缝，把整个院子围得严严实实。正屋翻修一新，门窗换了新的，屋顶铺了深灰色的瓦片。东边的厢房里住着两个马夫——年长的姓刘，四十出头，以前在城里的骡马行干过，对马的事门清，什么样脾气的马到他手里都服服帖帖；年轻的那个叫小六，不到二十，力气大，干活不惜力，每天天不亮就起来添草料、刷马背，比刘叔还勤快。两人都是老周从城外庄子上筛出来的，无亲无故，嘴严实，干了快两年从来没多问过一句话。每个月领完工钱，老老实实买米买油，日子过得安安稳稳。苏尘对这两个人很满意——他不需要多聪明的手下，他只要嘴严的。
西边的马厩里养着五匹马。两匹是苏烈让人从边关送来的军马，膘肥体壮，毛色油亮，一看就是在战场上跑过的料，脾气也烈，除了刘叔之外旁人靠近了就要打响鼻。三匹是普通马，品相差一些，但混在一起也看不出什么区别，平时给刘叔和小六代步用。仓库里堆着草料和工具，整整齐齐。刘叔是个细心人，草料垛得方方正正，地上扫得干干净净，连工具都按大小挂在墙上，比苏尘预期的还要利索。
从外面看，这就是一座普普通通的乡间马场，毫不起眼。
名堂全在地下。
密室这两年一直没停过工。第一年只挖了一间小室用来放杂物，后来发现地方根本不够用——这两年淘来的零碎材料，跟老周往来的记录都得有个稳妥的地方收着。于是第二年又往东边扩了一间，往北边再扩了一间。
现在地下已经有了三间小室，加上最早的正室，四间石室连成一片。
入口在正屋的床底下，掀开活动石板，沿着台阶往下走几步，最先到的是正室。三丈见方，青砖砌墙，横梁加固，顶上每隔两步就用一根立柱撑着，走在里面完全感觉不到是在地下。油灯放在墙角的一张矮桌上，灯芯是苏尘自己调的，用柏木油和少许桐油兑出来的，烟气少，耐用，添一次油能烧两三个时辰。

正室的东墙上开了一道门，通向第一间小室。这间最小，只有一丈见方多一点，里面放着一口小柜子。柜子里锁着几本从老周那里收来的杂书，里面有关于血修门派的零碎记载，也有几页抄录的草药方子——老周不知道从哪弄来的，只说“有用就收着“。柜子底层还有几件从黑市上淘来的低阶材料，品相一般，但胜在便宜，苏尘目前还用不上，留着以后总有用得着的时候。最底下是一小箱散碎的下品玄铢，是他这两年从月钱里一点一点省下来的。逢年过节长辈给的压岁钱、王妃随手塞的零花，他大多攒了下来，没怎么花。钱不多，但万一有急用，也不至于两手空空。
第十一章十二
北墙上的门通向第二间小室，比第一间稍大一些。里面放着一张木桌和一把椅子，桌上摊着一本翻开的无名中品功法残本。书页已经泛黄发脆，边角缺损了好几处，经脉图谱上有三分之一的部分是缺失的，剩下的线条也有些模糊。两年下来，苏尘已经把这本残本上能看懂的部分翻来覆去看了无数遍。凭借前世的经脉知识，大致的框架他已经能推个七七八八了。他有种直觉——这套功法跟血修门派脱不了干系。等修为到了凝元境，他打算试着推演一下缺失的部分。
最大的一间在最里面，紧挨着正室，被他收拾成了一间静室。地上铺了蒲团，墙角立着一盏油灯，空气干燥而安静。在这里引动龙脉气息，比在别的房间里都顺畅得多——脚下就是那条重叠龙脉，虽然以他现在的修为能吸收的量微乎其微，但那股温热的气息从地底缓缓渗上来，像是大地本身在呼吸，光是待在里面就让人觉得安定。有时候他不想回府，就在这里坐上一整夜，翻翻残本，运气几个周天，累了就靠着墙闭一会儿眼。
四间石室加起来，总面积比最初多了一倍。地方不算大，但该有的都有了——材料有地方放了，书有地方藏了，练功有专门的静室了。不用像头一年那样什么东西都挤在正室里，转个身都费劲。苏尘有时候会站在静室中央环顾一圈，心里盘算着下一轮扩建从哪里下手。三五年的时间，应该能把这片地下修成一个像样的据点。
等修为再高一些，需要的东西多了，这边还得继续扩。好在这块地皮够大，地下空间也足够，想扩随时可以动工。
苏尘离开马场，沿着官道往回走。
秋末的风带了寒意，吹在脸上有些发凉。路两边的麦子已经收完了，只剩下一片一片光秃秃的茬子，在暮色中像是大地的皱纹。他拢了拢衣领，脚步不快不慢地走着。远处朔州城墙的轮廓在暮色中显得厚重而沉默，城头的灯笼已经点上了，暖黄的光在风中轻轻摇晃。
走了大约两里路，迎面遇上一个人。
青萝。
两年过去，她也从小姑娘长成了大姑娘。个子拔高了一截，原先圆润的脸庞褪了些婴儿肥，有了几分清晰的轮廓，头上挽了一个简单的髻，比从前多了些稳重的味道。但一开口，那股熟悉的感觉就回来了。
“世子——！可算找着您了！“
苏尘脚步不停：“怎么了？“

Chapter 11 Twelve
When Su Chen came out of the secret room, it was already dark.
He stood at the exit for a few seconds, waiting for his eyes to adjust to the change in light, then bent down to cover the movable stone slab, and then dragged the bed board back to its original position. Everything was restored to its original state. From the outside, this main house looked no different from any ordinary country house.
He opened the door, walked out to the yard, and took a deep breath of the evening air.
I just sat in the secret room for nearly two hours, activating the dragon vein aura to complete eight small weeks. The moment he finished the exercise, he clearly felt that the energy in his Dantian sank suddenly, as if he had finally crossed an invisible threshold - the middle stage of the body tempering realm, and he had officially entered it.
The feeling at that moment was very subtle. It was as if I had been climbing a gentle slope. I couldn't feel any changes after climbing for a long time, but at an inadvertent moment I suddenly looked back and realized that I was already much taller than when I started. The vitality in the Dantian no longer needs to be deliberately maintained as before, but gathers together naturally, forming a stable cycle. Although the quantity is still not much, the quality is already different - like a ball of loose dough kneaded into a smooth dough.
It took two full years from entry to mid-term.
This speed cannot be said to be fast. The Naqi method is originally the worst thing on the market, and its energy absorption efficiency is pitifully low. Not to mention the first half of the year - the meridians are narrow and weak, and every time I introduce a trace of energy into the body, it is like drinking water through a thin straw. After a long time of effort, I can only take a small sip, and it will break if I am not careful. During that time, he practiced for two hours every day without hesitation, but the increase in vitality in his Dantian was almost invisible to the naked eye. Several times after practicing, he would sit on the futon and close his eyes to look inside. His Dantian was empty, as if he had never practiced. He understood that this was the only way to go - the secret technique practiced by Cao Qin in his previous life was also slow at the beginning, but it was a special route for eunuchs and was different from the normal route. Unexpectedly, after switching to the Naqi method, starting out was even more difficult than in the previous life. Sometimes after practicing all night, I feel lighter the next day than the day before, as if I have missed the little bit I finally saved. He knew in his heart that this was a normal phenomenon that the meridians had not yet adapted to the flow of energy. For several late nights, he sat alone on the futon in the secret room, feeling the faint trace of vitality in his Dantian. He couldn't help but think of the feeling of vitality rushing like a river in his previous life when Cao Qin was at his peak. In contrast, I now look like a child holding a wooden sword looking at the swordsman on the top of the mountain. But he just thought about it, sighed, and then retracted his thoughts and continued to exercise. He knew there was no point in rushing. He had already understood this path from his previous life - if the foundation was not strong, he would not be able to go far.
It took half a year for the results to really start to show results. The meridians gradually widen as they are polished day after day, just like a path that has been stepped on repeatedly, and it becomes wider as you walk. The flow of energy in the body becomes smoother and smoother, and it no longer stops at every turn. In the same two hours, I could barely complete one or two small weeks at first, but after half a year I could complete four or five. Then six, then seven - and by the last month, it had stabilized at eight. The mass of vitality in the Dantian has also grown from a vague trace at the beginning to a mass as thick as a little finger now. It has a solid and heavy feeling when it is running, and it does not scatter when the wind blows like it did at the beginning.
The overlapping dragon veins under the secret room also contributed a lot. Although the amount of stimulation each time is very small, over the course of two years, the little by little difference will be revealed unconsciously. Like a trickle, the amount of water is not large, but it continues all year round and can always water the fields. He sometimes thought that without this dragon vein, it would probably take another two years to reach the middle stage of the Body Tempering Realm by relying solely on the Qi-Napping Method. This secret under the racecourse is probably the biggest bargain he has ever picked up in his life.
According to this momentum, the body quenching state should not be perfect.It will take another two years. He made a rough calculation in his mind - it would be faster to reach perfection from the middle stage than to enter the middle stage, because the meridians have been opened, and the road ahead is just a matter of accumulation. You should be able to touch the threshold of perfection in about a year and a half. At that time, it’s time to consider breaking through to the Condensing Yuan Realm. After condensing the essence, there is opening of the meridians, and then the foundation.
The foundation-casting realm requires mid-level skills. The unnamed incomplete book in his hand now is of middle grade, but it is missing a few key pages, and it seems to be related to the blood cultivator sect. Whether, when and how to practice it must be carefully considered. But that's for later. Let’s take this step first before talking about it. Tall buildings rising from the ground - he understood this in his previous life, but he could only really do it in this life.
Su Chen walked down the steps, stretched his shoulders in the dusk, and walked casually around the yard.
In the past two years, the racecourse has completely changed its appearance. The fence is tall and solid, with blue bricks and joints, tightly surrounding the entire yard. The main house was renovated, the doors and windows were replaced with new ones, and the roof was paved with dark gray tiles. There are two grooms living in the east side room - the older one is named Liu and is in his early forties. He used to work in a mule and horse business in the city. He is very knowledgeable about horses and he will obey any horse of any temper. The younger one is called Xiao Liu, less than 20 years old. He is very strong and does not hesitate to work hard. He gets up before dawn every day to add fodder and brush the horses' backs. He is more diligent than Uncle Liu. Both of them were screened out by Lao Zhou from Zhuangzi outside the city. They were not related to each other, and they were strict-mouthed. They had never asked a question after working together for almost two years. After receiving the completion payment every month, he would buy rice and oil honestly, and live a stable life. Su Chen was very satisfied with these two people - he didn't need smart subordinates, he just wanted to be strict-mouthed.
The stables to the west house five horses. The two horses were sent by Su Lie from the border. They were fat and strong, with shiny coats. They looked like they had been on the battlefield. They also had a fierce temper and would sneeze at anyone except Uncle Liu who came near them. The three horses are ordinary horses with slightly different qualities, but you can't tell any difference when mixed together. They are usually used by Uncle Liu and Xiaoliu for transportation. The warehouse is neatly stacked with fodder and tools. Uncle Liu was a careful man. The stacks of hay were square and square, the floor was swept clean, and even the tools were hung on the wall according to size, which was neater than Su Chen expected.
From the outside, this is an ordinary country horse farm, unremarkable.
The fame is all underground.
The secret room has been under construction for the past two years. In the first year, I only dug a small room to store sundries, but later I found that the space was not enough - the scraps of materials collected in the past two years, and the records of contacts with Lao Zhou all had to be stored in a safe place. So the next year, one room was expanded to the east and another room to the north.
Now there are three small chambers underground, plus the earliest main chamber, four stone chambers are connected together.
The entrance is under the bed in the main room. Open the movable stone slab and walk down a few steps. The first thing you arrive at is the main room. It is three feet square, with green brick walls and reinforced beams. The top is supported by a pillar every two steps. When you walk inside, you don't feel like you are underground. The oil lamp was placed on a low table in the corner. The wick was adjusted by Su Chen himself. It was made from cypress oil and a little tung oil. It had little smoke and was durable. It could burn for two or three hours once the oil was added.
A door was opened on the east wall of the main room, leading to the first small room. This room is the smallest, just over one foot square, with a small cabinet inside. Locked in the cabinet were several miscellaneous books collected from Lao Zhou, which contained fragmentary records about the Blood Cultivation Sect, as well as a few pages of transcribed herbal prescriptions - Lao Zhou didn't know where they got them from, so he only said, "Keep them if they are useful." There are a few low-end materials from the black market on the bottom floor of the cabinet. They are of average quality, but they are cheap. Su Chen can't use them yet, but he will keep them for later when he will need them. At the bottom is a small box of scattered low-grade xuan baht, which he has saved bit by bit from his monthly money in the past two years.of. He saved most of the New Year's money given by his elders during the holidays and the pocket money that the princess randomly stuffed into him, and did not spend much. It’s not a lot of money, but if you need it urgently, you won’t be left empty-handed.
Chapter 11 Twelve
A door in the north wall leads to a second cell, slightly larger than the first. There was a wooden table and a chair inside. On the table lay an open fragment of an unknown middle-grade skill. The pages are yellowed and brittle, with several corners missing. One-third of the meridian map is missing, and the remaining lines are somewhat blurry. Over the past two years, Su Chen has read through the understandable parts of this fragmented book countless times. With the knowledge of meridians from his previous life, he could already deduce the general framework. He had an intuition that this set of exercises was closely related to the Blood Cultivation Sect. When his cultivation reached the Condensing Yuan realm, he planned to try to deduce the missing parts.
The largest room was in the innermost room, next to the main room, and he had packed it into a quiet room. There was a futon on the floor, an oil lamp stood in the corner, and the air was dry and quiet. Inducing the dragon's breath here is much smoother than in other rooms - there is the overlapping dragon's veins under his feet. Although the amount he can absorb is very small with his current cultivation level, the warm breath slowly seeps up from the ground, as if the earth itself is breathing. Just staying in it makes people feel stable. Sometimes he didn't want to go back home, so he would just sit here all night, flipping through some scraps of books. After a few days of luck, he would lean against the wall and close his eyes for a while.
The total area of ​​the four stone rooms doubled from the original. The place is not big, but it has everything it needs - there is a place to put the materials, a place to hide the books, and a special quiet room for practicing. There was no need to squeeze everything into the main room like the previous year, and it was difficult to turn around. Su Chen would sometimes stand in the middle of the quiet room and look around, thinking about where to start the next round of expansion. In three to five years, this underground area should be able to be built into a decent stronghold.
When the cultivation level is higher and more things are needed, we will have to continue to expand here. Fortunately, the land is large enough and there is enough underground space, so we can start construction at any time if we want to expand.
Su Chen left the racecourse and walked back along the official road.
The late autumn wind brought a chill, which made my face feel chilly. The wheat harvest on both sides of the road has been finished, leaving only patches of bare stubble, which look like wrinkles on the earth in the dusk. He tightened his collar and walked neither fast nor slow. The outline of the Shuozhou City Wall in the distance looked thick and silent in the dusk. The lanterns at the top of the city had been lit, and the warm yellow light swayed gently in the wind.
After walking about two miles, I met a person head-on.
Green radish.
Two years have passed, and she has grown from a little girl to a big girl. He has grown taller, and his originally round face has lost some of the baby fat, gaining a somewhat clear outline. He wears a simple bun on his head, giving him a more stable look than before. But as soon as he opened his mouth, that familiar feeling came back.
"Your Majesty——! I have finally found you!"
Su Chen kept walking: "What's wrong?"
